name: Better Than a Thousand
label: Revelation
lede: Two guys from Battery made a youth crew demo for fun, handed the mic to Ray Cappo on a break from Shelter, and ended up touring four continents on a side project nobody rehearsed for.

eras.title: A demo that got out of hand
eras.text: When Battery broke up, drummer Ken Olden and guitarist Graham Land wanted to bring back the late-'80s youth crew sound. They asked the man who had defined it, Youth of Today's Ray Cappo, who was still fronting Shelter. What started as a few songs in an Atlanta studio became a Revelation album within the year.

years.h: Ex-Battery pair Ken Olden and Graham Land cut a demo in Atlanta
years.p: After [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]] split, Olden and Land record hardcore songs at Issa Diao's studio in Atlanta. Diao played in [[Good Clean Fun|a0e64a50-4480-495b-b98e-2e766b12ea8c]].

years.cap: Better Than a Thousand · via Discogs
years.h: Ray Cappo signs on between Shelter tours
years.p: Olden and Land recruit [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]] of Youth of Today and Shelter, whom Olden first met at a Youth of Today show in Washington, D.C., in 1988. Jeff Neumann joins on bass.

years.src: Revelation Records · Revelation Records pressing history · Wikipedia: Just One
years.h: Just One, Better Than a Thousand's debut · REV 60
years.p: Made in five days during a Shelter break, with Ray Cappo singing his parts in a bedroom studio in two days. Revelation's bio says you can hear his voice getting hoarse by the end.
years.xp: Twelve songs, none longer than 2:40, with artwork by Tom Bejgrowicz. Revelation pressed 2,029 on black and 517 on clear, and Wikipedia says the band built a large following off it.

eras.title: Value driven, then gone
eras.text: Better Than a Thousand toured harder than most full-time bands: America, Europe, Asia and South America. The second album was made in Ken Olden's bedroom and bathroom, and when Cappo moved to California the band simply stopped.

years.h: Value Driven: recorded in Ken Olden's bedroom and bathroom
years.p: The second Better Than a Thousand album opens with Demand Independence, the song Olden picks as the band's best. Another track opens with a clip of Gandhi speaking on nonviolence.

q: Most of our shows were packed
years.h: Better Than a Thousand tour four continents without rehearsing
years.p: Better Than a Thousand play America, Europe, Asia and South America behind Value Driven. Ken Olden says the songs were simple enough that they could tour without rehearsing.
years.xp: Olden says the band was more about energy and message than chops, and that most of its shows were packed.

years.h: Self Worth: Better Than a Thousand's last single
years.p: The Self Worth single comes out on Grapes of Wrath, the band's last new release.

years.h: Ray Cappo moves to California and Better Than a Thousand end
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Cappo relocated to California and quit the straight edge lifestyle, and the band broke up. He turned toward teaching yoga.

eras.title: Remastered, with a fanzine
eras.text: Better Than a Thousand never reunited, but the records kept coming back: a Record Store Day repress of Just One and then a deluxe reissue of both albums that Ken Olden remixed himself.

years.h: Just One repressed for Record Store Day
years.p: Revelation re-presses Better Than a Thousand's Just One: 772 on opaque red for Record Store Day and 328 on opaque grey.

q: Better Than a Thousand did so much more than we ever imagined
years.h: End Hits reissues Just One and Value Driven
years.p: Ken Olden remixes and remasters both Better Than a Thousand albums, adding new guitar and five rare bonus songs, for End Hits Records.
years.xp: The package came with a 36-page fanzine of unpublished photos and liner notes, and the CD was limited to 500 copies. Olden, looking back, sounded surprised by how far it went.
